$comment: Single source of truth for the SQL guard. 'rejected' statements must fail with CURF_SQL_REJECTED and change nothing, even on a writable account. 'accepted' statements must run read-only on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQL Server; an entry's 'variants' give the text to use instead of 'sql' on a database whose syntax differs (Oracle needs FROM dual and has its columns in lower case inside quotes). Table 'guard_probe'(id int primary key, label varchar(50)) with 3 rows exists in the test databases.

rejected.sql: SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2; DELETE FROM guard_probe
WITH x AS (DELETE FROM guard_probe RETURNING id) SELECT * FROM x
WITH x AS (INSERT INTO guard_probe VALUES (99, 'x') RETURNING id) SELECT * FROM x
WITH x AS (UPDATE guard_probe SET label = 'x' RETURNING id) SELECT * FROM x
ALTER TABLE guard_probe ADD COLUMN b int
GRANT ALL ON guard_probe TO PUBLIC
SELECT * FROM (SELECT pg_read_file('/etc/passwd') AS f) s
WITH x AS (SELECT pg_read_file('/etc/passwd') AS f) SELECT * FROM x
SELECT 1 WHERE pg_read_file('/etc/passwd') IS NOT NULL
SELECT * FROM dblink('host=x', 'select 1') AS t(a int)

variants.ORACLE: SELECT 'x' AS into_label, 1 AS update_flag FROM dual

accepted.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 'delete' ELSE 'insert' END AS c

variants.ORACLE: SELECT CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 'delete' ELSE 'insert' END AS c FROM dual
SELECT 1 FROM dual -- ; DROP TABLE guard_probe

accepted.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT n FROM a

variants.ORACLE: WITH a AS (SELECT 1 AS n FROM dual) SELECT n FROM a

accepted.sql: WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM r

variants.ORACLE: WITH r(n) AS (SELECT 1 FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM r
variants.SQLSERVER: WITH r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM r

accepted.sql: SELECT n, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY n) AS rn FROM (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2) s

variants.ORACLE: SELECT n, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY n) AS rn FROM (SELECT 1 AS n FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 2 FROM dual) s

accepted.sql: SELECT 1 AS a UNION ALL SELECT 2

variants.ORACLE: SELECT 1 AS a FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 2 FROM dual

accepted.sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS a) s WHERE a IN (SELECT 1)

variants.ORACLE: SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 AS a FROM dual) s WHERE a IN (SELECT 1 FROM dual)

accepted.sql: SELECT count(*) AS c FROM guard_probe
SELECT id, label FROM guard_probe WHERE id = :id
